dedupe_keys.name: flood induced traffic disruption model for hospital access in germany hidden risks in healthcare

description: This model estimates which hospitals in Germany would face delayed emergency access or sudden patient surges when floods cut roads and push traffic onto detours, even if the hospitals themselves stay dry. It couples flood events from a regional flood model, downscaled to 5 m rasters, with a gravity-based traffic model on the OpenStreetMap road network, using population from the Global Human Settlement Layer and travel behaviour from the German Mobility Panel, and recomputes flows and hospital catchments when flooded roads close. The producers are Jonas Wassmer and co-authors at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research and the University of Potsdam, who report in Communications Earth & Environment (2025) that 75 of 2,475 hospitals are at risk of surges beyond normal capacity from flood-related traffic disruption alone, a third of them more than 10 km from any inundation. Coverage is Germany. The code, precomputed road network loads, flood rasters and interactive maps are on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0 as a 21 GB package; users must download OpenStreetMap, population and mobility panel data themselves. Caveats: computing loads for new areas needs high-performance computing, the README does not state the programming language or dependencies, the mobility panel must be ordered, and a correction to the article was published in 2026. Simulation uses: national screening of hospitals exposed to indirect flood impacts, emergency route planning, and scenario tests for ambulance access. Related records: OpenEMS (model-openems-ambulance-deployment) optimises ambulance locations, and AccessMod (model-accessmod) computes health access under disrupted roads.
